raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Validate draft-token capacity in `vllm bench forward` before preparing a case's inputs. Fixes #61766: a verify case requiring three draft tokens currently reaches CUDA execution even when the runner has zero draft capacity.

## Claims

- Reject cases whose draft count exceeds the runner's resolved `num_speculative_steps`, with a case-specific `ValueError` and a `--speculative-config` hint.
- Preserve execution for ordinary decode and verify cases with sufficient capacity.
- Cover missing and insufficient capacity in the existing benchmark test suite, and document the requirement in the microbenchmark skill.

## Validation

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selected benchmark regression tests | 2 failed, 2 passed | 4 passed, 1 deselected |
| L4: `verify=2*4@64:3`, no speculative config | CUDA illegal memory access | Expected `ValueError`, no illegal memory access |
| L4: `decode=2*1@64` | Passed | Passed |
| L4: same verify, configured draft capacity 3 | Passed | Passed |

The patched GPU controls use the same publicly exported random Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint. Both successful cases have finite, deterministic outputs and graph-versus-eager relative RMS difference 0. These are correctness smoke checks, not model-quality or performance measurements.

The existing model-dependent pytest end-to-end case was deselected; three separate benchmark CLI runs provided GPU coverage. New tests live in `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py`, already included in the Buildkite benchmarks CLI job.

Commands executed (validation scripts are in the separate archive branch):

```bash
UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-audit-uv-cache uv run --no-project --python 3.12 \
  --with 'modal[api-proxy-support]' --with huggingface_hub \
  modal run reproductions/forward-verify-2026-10-15/validate_modal.py::check \
  --model-revision 4bae0ac45199180f8d59d05bb3b6cc1b19c58357

UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-audit-uv-cache PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/tmp/vllm-audit-precommit \
  uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with pre-commit \
  pre-commit run --files vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py .agents/skills/model-microbenchmark/SKILL.md
```

Pre-commit passed, including Ruff, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and skill validation.

Environment: one NVIDIA L4 on Modal, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Python source at `c5f8adc0b1944b9142a31d85cfbc6a61973d0b3a` was overlaid on compiled extensions and generated wrappers from an official vLLM image reporting `0.32.0rc1.dev100+g77154ca61`. This is composite source/runtime validation, not a full build from that source commit. Source/runtime provenance is recorded separately in the archive.

- [Scripts, original logs, synthetic inputs, and validation receipts](https://github.com/znzryb/vllm/tree/contribution-rules-and-bug-audit/reproductions/forward-verify-2026-10-15)
- [Public random checkpoint, pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/znzryb/qwen3-0.6b-dummy-forward-repro/tree/4bae0ac45199180f8d59d05bb3b6cc1b19c58357)
- [Public raw data and validation logs, pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/znzryb/vllm-forward-verify-repro/tree/239159c4fdaaf568fe9c00153cbfbf57ab1bf8bc)

## Details

The benchmark builds scheduler inputs directly. Without speculative configuration, the observed runner has `num_speculative_steps=0` and a draft-token buffer of shape `[4, 0]`, yet the verify case schedules three draft tokens per request. The missing consistency check lets this invalid combination enter GPU input preparation. CUDA errors are asynchronous; no exact faulting kernel is claimed.

The guard runs at the start of `run_case`, before batch construction and input preparation, using resolved runner capacity rather than requiring a particular CLI configuration. Engine initialization still precedes the check. This is benchmark configuration validation; it does not change a CUDA kernel or repair computation under a valid configuration.

Duplicate checks: read #61766 and searched open PRs for the issue number and `bench forward`. No overlapping fix was found. #61692 adds profiling, not draft-capacity validation. The three affected files are unchanged on the latest upstream main checked before submission.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, reproduction scripts, and executing the reported checks. The human submitter reviewed the proposed change in the associated discussion and authorized submission; the test executions reported here were performed by the agent.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -31,6 +31,9 @@ Requests: `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]`, comma-separated, per DP rank.
 | `2048@10240` | prefill after an 8192-token prefix-cache hit |
 | `2048@10240c` | chunked prefill: the prefix came from earlier chunks |
 
+Verify cases require `--speculative-config` with `num_speculative_tokens`
+at least as large as the case's draft count; insufficient capacity is rejected.
+
 Hit vs chunk only differs on models with SWA bounded replay (DSV4.1): a hit
 also recomputes the last window (128 tokens) of the prefix.

@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@
 import pytest
 
 from vllm.benchmarks.forward.batch import build_batch
+from vllm.benchmarks.forward.main import run_case
 from vllm.benchmarks.forward.shapes import jitter_kv_lens, parse_case
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 
@@ -84,6 +85,18 @@ def test_jitter_kv_lens():
         jitter_kv_lens(case, 0, 1000, 0)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("capacity", [0, 2])
+def test_bench_forward_rejects_oversized_verify(capacity):
+    """Reject drafts beyond the runner's buffer before launching CUDA kernels."""
+    runner = SimpleNamespace(num_speculative_steps=capacity)
+    case = parse_case("verify=2*4@64:3")
+    with pytest.raises(
+        ValueError,
+        match=rf"Case 'verify' needs 3 draft tokens.*supports {capacity}",
+    ):
+        run_case(runner, case, SimpleNamespace())
+
+
 @pytest.mark.benchmark
 # TODO(woosuk): Support ROCm and re-enable this test there.
 @pytest.mark.skipif(

@@ -120,6 +120,14 @@ def _make_engine_args(args: argparse.Namespace, cases: list[BenchCase]):
 
 
 def run_case(runner, case: BenchCase, args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    required_drafts = max((r.num_draft_tokens for r in case.requests), default=0)
+    if required_drafts > runner.num_speculative_steps:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Case {case.name!r} needs {required_drafts} draft tokens per request, "
+            f"but the runner supports {runner.num_speculative_steps}. "
+            "Set --speculative-config with a sufficient num_speculative_tokens."
+        )
+
     from vllm.benchmarks.forward.batch import build_batch
     from vllm.benchmarks.forward.capture import ForwardBench
     from vllm.benchmarks.forward.kv_init import touched_kv_views, zero_kv_blocks
